prompt: I run a tiny creative studio called Northlight (3 people, Oslo) — we do brand identities and motion for music festivals and outdoor brands. I want our new site to feel like an Awwwards site of the day, not a template. Home page only for now: intro, selected work (4 projects, make them up), what we do, and contact. Smooth scrolling and proper animation please. One index.html, CDN libraries are fine.
assertions: index.html honours prefers-reduced-motion by disabling or simplifying its motion (CSS media query or JS matchMedia check)
index.html's main headline and body copy are visible with JavaScript disabled (nothing essential is left hidden by CSS waiting for a script)
index.html loads with no console errors
index.html animates only transform, opacity, clip-path or filter — no per-frame animation of top/left/width/height/margin
index.html has no horizontal page scroll at a 390px-wide viewport
index.html varies entrance motion by element role (at least two distinct reveal treatments, e.g. line/mask reveal for headlines and scale/clip for media), rather than one identical fade-up everywhere
index.html uses no emoji and no default purple/indigo-to-blue/pink gradient
index.html implements smooth scrolling (Lenis or an equivalent) that keeps native scroll and anchor links working
index.html includes intro, 4 selected projects, a what-we-do section and contact details
index.html has a clearly identifiable signature moment (one standout interaction or scroll scene) rather than evenly distributed effects
